subject: A shaggy Highland cow standing in tall summer grass on a hillside at sunset, with blue hills, a glimpse of a loch, and a gold-and-blue sky behind it.
focal_point: The cow's face: the glowing fringe falling over its eyes and the rosy muzzle below it, framed by the two curved horns.
light: A low sun behind the cow and off to the right, past the hills. It turns the sky gold and orange on the right, and puts a glowing gold rim on the top and right-hand edges of the cow's coat, its fringe and the tops of its horns, and on the tips of the tall grass.
why: Work back to front: the sunset sky and its clouds, the two blue ranges and the loch, then the green hillside and the meadow base, so the cow has finished ground behind it. The cow then gets most of the steps the way a teacher builds a shaggy animal: a rust shape from pieces, the dark side, copper and then gold locks, the sunlit rim, and the face last. The tall grass goes on after the cow because it stands in front of its legs, dark blades first and the bright seed heads last.

things.name: The sunset sky
things.why: A smooth sky from clear blue at the top to gold and orange low on the right, blended wet in one go.

things.name: The sunlit cloud streaks
things.why: Soft gold and orange streaks painted over the dry sky, lit from below by the low sun.
things.left_out: The brightest-edge pass; the light tops are enough at this distance.

things.name: The far blue mountains
things.why: A pale, soft blue-violet range with no texture, the farthest land.
things.left_out: Separate shadow and light passes; at this distance the range reads as one flat shape.

things.name: The nearer blue hills
things.why: A darker blue-violet range overlapping the far one, still simple and soft.
things.left_out: Separate shadow and light passes; it stays a few big shapes.

things.name: The loch
things.why: A small pale strip of water at the right, at the foot of the blue hills; only its base is needed.
things.left_out: Light streaks and ripples; it is too small and far to show them.

things.name: The green hillside behind the cow
things.why: The sloping middle-ground field, laid in as a base from yellow-green to olive; its texture is the scrub patches.
things.left_out: Grass flicks; the hillside is too far back for blades.

things.name: The dark scrub patches on the hillside
things.why: Low bushes and heather clumps read as dabbed dark foliage on the slope.
things.left_out: Middle and sunlit dabs; the yellow-green hillside between the patches is their light.

things.name: The tall grass meadow
things.why: The foreground grass: a base lighter at the back and darker in front, then flicked blades in passes, darkest first, ending in the sunlit seed heads.

things.name: The Highland cow
things.why: A long-haired animal whose coat hangs in locks, with a sunlit rim and the face last: exactly this element.
things.left_out: Single hairs and wisps, and the eyes themselves; the fringe covers them, so only a shadowy dark peeks out under it. The legs are left as rough pieces because the grass covers them.

things.name: The curved horns
things.why: Two curved, tapering horns with a shadow side and a lit top edge, built from pieces; the shaggy element has no step for horns.

paints.name: Sky blue
paints.looks: a soft mid blue: ultramarine and white with a touch of burnt sienna to calm it

paints.name: Pale gold
paints.looks: white with a little yellow, the lightest warm color in the painting

paints.name: Warm orange
paints.looks: yellow, a little red and a little white: a glowing sunset orange

paints.name: Bright gold
paints.looks: yellow with a touch of burnt sienna: a strong warm golden yellow

paints.name: Pale blue-violet
paints.looks: Blue-violet plus plenty of white: a hazy, light blue-violet for the farthest mountains

paints.name: Blue-violet
paints.looks: ultramarine, a touch of red and white: a cool, deeper blue-violet

paints.name: Pale sky blue
paints.looks: Sky blue plus more white: a pale, glinting blue-white

paints.name: Yellow-green
paints.looks: yellow with a little ultramarine and white: a sunny light green

paints.name: Olive green
paints.looks: yellow, ultramarine and a little burnt sienna: a warm mid green

paints.name: Dark green
paints.looks: Olive green with more ultramarine and burnt sienna: a deep, shadowy green

paints.name: Rust brown
paints.looks: burnt sienna with a little red and yellow: the cow's warm reddish-brown coat

paints.name: Deep brown
paints.looks: burnt sienna with ultramarine: a near-black warm brown

paints.name: Copper
paints.looks: Rust brown with more yellow and a little white: a bright copper orange

paints.name: Horn gray
paints.looks: white with a little burnt sienna and ultramarine: a warm gray-brown

paints.name: Rosy brown
paints.looks: Rust brown with white and a touch of red: a dusky pinkish brown

paints.name: Pale rosy brown
paints.looks: Rosy brown plus white: a light pinkish tan

steps.name: Blend the sunset sky

lays.what: the whole sky from the top edge down past the hill line to about a third of the way down the canvas: sky blue at the top, fading to pale gold lower down, with warm orange low on the right where the sun is

steps.after: The top third of the canvas is a smooth sky: blue at the top, pale gold below it, glowing orange low on the right. It runs a little below where the hills will go. Everything below is bare white canvas.
steps.why: Farthest away, and it has to be wet-blended in one go before anything sits on it.

steps.name: Dry-brush the cloud streaks

lays.what: long, soft, flat-bottomed streaks across the sky: bright gold streaks at the upper left and across the middle, warm orange streaks lower on the right near the sun

steps.after: Soft, broken gold streaks cross the blue at the upper left and middle of the sky, and orange streaks lie low on the right. The blue and gold sky shows through their edges. The rest of the canvas is still bare.

steps.name: Light the tops of the clouds

lays.what: the lower and right-hand edges of each streak that face the sun, in pale gold, leaving the darker gold in the middle of each

steps.after: Each cloud streak now has a pale gold lit edge on the side toward the sun, with its darker gold or orange still showing in the middle. The sky is finished; the land is still bare.

stages.name: The far hills and the loch

steps.name: Lay in the far mountains

lays.what: the farthest range of rounded mountains across the canvas just below the sky, a band about one-tenth of the canvas tall, its top edge a soft wavy line

steps.after: A pale, hazy blue-violet mountain line sits across the canvas under the sky, soft-edged and flat. Below it the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Lay in the nearer blue hills

lays.what: the nearer hills overlapping the bottom of the far range, rising on the left and dipping toward the right, down to about three-tenths of the way down the canvas

steps.after: A deeper blue-violet range now overlaps the pale one, so the hills step back in two layers. Everything below the hills is bare.

steps.name: Lay in the loch

lays.what: a short, thin strip of water at the right edge, at the foot of the nearer hills, about a quarter of the canvas wide

steps.after: A pale, glinting strip of loch lies at the right edge under the blue hills. The background is finished; the lower two-thirds are bare.

steps.name: Lay in the green hillside

lays.what: the slope from the foot of the blue hills down to about halfway down the canvas, high on the left and dropping to the right, straight through where the cow will stand: olive green near the hills, yellow-green where the sun lights it lower down

steps.after: A green slope fills the middle band, olive at the top against the blue hills and sunny yellow-green lower down, with its edge cutting just under the loch. It is still flat with no patches; the bottom half is bare.

steps.name: Dab the dark scrub patches

lays.what: scattered rounded patches of dark scrub across the hillside, smaller and closer together toward the hills, larger on the lower slope, with yellow-green showing between them

steps.after: The hillside is dotted with dark green patches with sunny green between them, so it reads as rough ground falling away. The bottom half of the canvas is still bare.

steps.name: Blend the meadow base

lays.what: the whole lower half of the canvas, straight through where the cow will go: yellow-green at the top where it meets the hillside, blending to olive green at the bottom

steps.after: The whole canvas is covered. The lower half is a smooth meadow, sunny yellow-green at the top fading to olive at the bottom, with no blades yet.

steps.name: Darken the front of the meadow

lays.what: the bottom third of the canvas and the lower corners, in loose level strokes, thinning out as they go up

steps.after: The meadow now goes from light at the back to a deep green at the bottom edge. It is still flat; the cow's place is still just grass.

steps.name: Build the cow from pieces

lays.what: the whole cow in rust brown: a big tall oval for the body left of center, from just below the hill line to about three-quarters of the way down; the head as a smaller rounded shape on its upper right; the fringe as a curved cap over the head; an ear on each side under where the horns go; and short leg pieces at the bottom, every stroke curving down the way the hair hangs

steps.after: A flat rust-brown cow shape stands left of center over the meadow: big body, rounded head with a fringe cap and two ears, rough legs at the bottom. No light, no locks, no face, no horns yet.

steps.name: Build the horns

lays.what: two curved horns from the top of the head: the left one sweeping out and up to a point over the hills, the right one out sideways and curling up to a point, each a wide piece at the head and a narrower curved piece to the tip

steps.after: Two flat gray-brown horns curve up from the cow's head against the blue hills. They have no shading yet.

steps.name: Shade the cow's dark side

lays.what: long downward curves of deep brown on the left of the body, under the fringe and the chin, behind the ears, down the chest and low on the belly and legs, leaving the rust showing on the right and top

steps.after: The cow now has a dark side: deep brown on the left and underneath, under the chin and fringe, rust still showing on the upper right. It looks round but smooth, with no locks.

steps.name: Shade the underside of the horns

lays.what: the underside of each horn and the base where it meets the head, in curves that follow each horn and fade out before the tip

steps.after: Each horn is dark at its base and along its lower edge, gray-brown along the top. The tips are still plain gray.

steps.name: Pull the copper locks

lays.what: long tapering locks hanging down over the body, the fringe falling over the eyes, and the ears, wide where each starts and pointed where it ends, with gaps so the rust and deep brown show between; fewer on the dark left side

steps.after: The coat now hangs in copper locks over the rust and dark brown, with the darks showing between them. The fringe is a curtain of copper locks over the face. The coat looks shaggy but not yet sunlit.

steps.name: Pull the golden locks

lays.what: fewer, shorter gold locks on the top and right of the body, the fringe and the right side of the face, over the copper, each covering less than the copper did

steps.after: Gold locks now catch the light on the top and right of the cow and through the fringe, with copper, rust and deep brown showing between them. The left side stays mostly dark. The edges still have no glow, and the face is still blank.

stages.name: The sunlit rim and the face

steps.name: Catch the sunlight on the rim and horns

lays.what: short tapering pale gold strokes running off the top of the fringe, the top of the back, the right edge of the face and chest and the wisps by the right ear
a thin pale gold line along the upper edge of each horn toward the tip, and the tips themselves

steps.after: The cow glows: a broken pale gold rim runs along the top of its fringe and back and down its right side, and the tops and tips of both horns shine pale. The muzzle is still plain rust under the fringe.
steps.why: The low sun lights the hair and the horns at once; with the brush loaded with pale gold and nearly dry, the painter skims every edge that faces the sun in one pass. Light over dark: two or three thin passes with drying between.

steps.name: Shape the muzzle

lays.what: the rounded muzzle under the fringe, a wide oval with curved strokes around it, and the chin just under it

steps.after: A rosy brown muzzle sits under the fringe on the right of the head, rounded, with the chin beneath. It has no nostrils or light yet.

steps.name: Light the top of the muzzle

lays.what: the top of the muzzle and the right side of the nose that face the sun, in short curves, leaving the rosy brown below

steps.after: The muzzle is round: light on its top and right, rosy brown below. Still no nostrils, mouth or eye.

steps.name: Line the nostrils, mouth and eye

lays.what: the two nostrils as small dark commas on the front of the nose, the short curved mouth line under them, and the dark of the left eye peeking out under the fringe

steps.after: The face is finished: two dark nostrils, a short mouth line and a shadowy eye just showing under the fringe. The cow is done except where the grass will cover its legs.

steps.name: Flick the dark grass blades

lays.what: upward blades across the meadow, longer and denser toward the bottom, and up over the bottom of the cow's coat and legs so it stands in the grass; few on the far meadow

steps.after: Dark green blades rise across the meadow and over the cow's legs, thick at the bottom and thinning upward. The meadow now has texture, still dark and without sunlit blades.

steps.name: Flick the sunny green blades

lays.what: fewer, lighter blades over the dark ones across the foreground and up over the cow's lower legs, leaving the dark showing between

steps.after: Sunny green blades now sit over the dark ones, so the grass has depth. No golden seed heads yet.

steps.name: Flick the golden seed heads

lays.what: the sunlit seed heads: short gold flicks scattered over the foreground meadow, bigger and farther apart toward the bottom, smaller toward the hillside, and a few in front of the cow's lower body and legs

steps.after: Bright gold seed heads glitter across the meadow and in front of the cow's legs, with the green and dark blades showing between. The painting is finished.
